script.title: How a Dog Hole Led Four Teens to Lascaux Cave
sentences: Four teenagers crawled down a tree hole into a seventeen-thousand-year-old art gallery.
In September 1940, Marcel Ravidat was walking his dog, Robot, in southwestern France.
The dog began sniffing an opening left by an uprooted tree.
Marcel returned with three friends, hoping for a legendary tunnel to a nearby manor.
Instead, the boys squeezed down a fifty-foot shaft into pitch blackness.
When they lit their lights, the stone walls were alive.
They were surrounded by over six hundred paintings of charging bulls, horses, and stags.
All because an eighteen-year-old followed his dog into the ground.
script.description: In 1940, four French teenagers followed a dog into a dark shaft. They had just stumbled into the world's greatest prehistoric art gallery.
visuals: Lascaux Hall of the Bulls cave painting

claims_en: Four teenagers crawled down a 50-foot shaft into a prehistoric cave.
In September 1940, Marcel Ravidat walked his dog Robot in southwestern France.
The dog investigated an opening created by an uprooted tree.
Marcel Ravidat returned with three friends believing the hole might lead to a secret manor passage.
The teenagers lowered themselves into a 50-foot shaft.
The cave walls were covered in prehistoric paintings.
The Lascaux cave contains over 600 paintings depicting bulls, horses, and stags.
The paintings date back approximately 17,000 years.
